text.p: These are the leading stories in Friday's Pakistani newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not an ch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The government has decided to enact new laws for setting up special courts to curb the growing spectre of sectarian and communal violence.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said a breakthrough has been achieved in talks with his Indian counterpart to resolve the Kashmir dispute through peaceful means.
- The state-run Karachi Electric Supply Corporation is on the verge of administrative and financial bankruptcy, Minister of Water and Power told the National Assembly (lower house).
- Pakistan rejected a charge by Uzbek President Islam Karimov that it was prolonging the civil war in Afghanistan by aiding the Taliban militia.

- The budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) is likely to focus on accelerating the rate of growth, bringing down inflation to around nine and 10 percent, reducing the budget deficit to less than six percent and narrowing the current account deficit by at least two billion rupees, sources said.
- Germany, Britain and seven other European Union members rejected calls for tough anti-dumping duties on unbleached cotton fabric exports from Pakistan and other Asian countries.
- Encouraged by the government's economic reforms, businessmen have ordered the import of more than 3,000 shuttleless looms, the Commerce Minister said.
- Indian officials said Pakistan has yet to give permission to conduct a route survey for the proposed $5.0 billion Iran-India gas pipeline which would run through its territory.

- Farmers' ability to meet the input cost of the next cotton crop would be badly impaired if payments running into billions of rupees held up by ginners due to unsold stocks of 1.8 million 375-lb bales are not made immediately, sources said.
- Over 700,000 tonnes of wheat and its by products are smuggled annually from the province of Punjab alone to neighbouring Afghanistan, sources said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has asked the International Monetary Fund to help work out the impact of its economic reforms programme and in fixing targets for the next fiscal year, sources said..
- The World Bank has stopped disbursement of a $93 million loan under the energy sector management assistance programme to Pakistan, sources said.

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has directed the Ministry of Water and Power, the provincial governments and the state-run Private Power and Infrastructure Board to speed up processing of major hydro-electric power projects of over 300 megawatts.
- With commissioning of more private power plants, oil demand will shoot up 94 percent to 11.7 tonnes in fiscal 1997/98 from the present six million tonnes, sources said.
FINANCIAL POST
- Liquid foreign exchange reserves, excluding gold, rose to $1.0919 billion on May 10, from $867.76 million on May 3, the State (central) Bank of Pakistan said.
NEWS
- The Water and Power Development Authority notified Hubco that it was terminating its power purchase agreement on the charges of alleged tampering with the meters.
- Pakistan has asked the United States to withdraw three Drug Enforcement Agency officials attached to the U.S. embassy in Islamabad.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif termed his talks with his Indian counterpart in Male as a "breakthrough".
- The government put off its plan to bring a constitutional amendment to curb terrorism, sectarianism and other heinous crimes.
- Senator Ishtiaq Azhar of the Mohajir Qaumi Movement (MQM) was acquitted in a murder case by a local court in Karachi.
THE NATION

- The Prime Minister's Accountability cell unearthed a sex scandal involving Asif Ali Zardari, husband of former prime minister and executives of a private bank which defrauded a state-owned bank of billions of rupees.
- The Lahore High Court has invalidated the exit control list restricting certain citizens from proceeding abroad.
- The Natioanl Assembly witnessed uproar over the reports that Benazir Bhutto was seeking asylum in Britain
THE MUSLIM
- The Accountability Commission referred a case against a sitting Senator of the ruling party alleging that he had defrauded a family of 1.2 million rupees to law directors for further scrutiny
- A joint investigation team probing the heroin smuggling case allegedly by two officers of Pakistan Air Force will soon complete its report.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
